content.value_statement: Java teams need clear examples for Azure Monitor logs and metrics. This skill provides SDK patterns for Kusto queries, metrics, batching, options, and migration.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency options for the deprecated azure-monitor-query package.
Explains LogsQueryClient and MetricsQueryClient creation with DefaultAzureCredential.
Provides examples for workspace, resource, batch, multi-workspace, and metrics queries.
Documents options for time intervals, aggregations, statistics, visualization, and timeouts.
Summarizes response shapes and basic error handling for partial failures.
Points users toward newer logs and metrics package migration guides.
limitations: Covers the deprecated Azure Monitor Query package, not the newer split packages in depth.
Does not run queries, authenticate, or inspect Azure environments.
Uses placeholders for workspace IDs, resource IDs, endpoints, and metric names.
Does not provide production-ready authorization, retry, or cost governance policies.

use_cases.title: Prototype Log Queries
use_cases.description: Create a Java query flow for Log Analytics workspace data using Kusto Query Language examples.

use_cases.title: Review Metrics Integration
use_cases.description: Compare metrics query patterns for one resource, multiple resources, aggregations, and time granularity.

use_cases.title: Plan SDK Migration
use_cases.description: Identify deprecated package usage and outline migration work toward the newer logs and metrics packages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Logs Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for Log Analytics queries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, explain how to create a Java LogsQueryClient with DefaultAzureCredential and query one workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Query Resource Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, show the steps to query Azure resource metrics with MetricsQueryClient, metric names, and a resource ID placeholder.

prompt_templates.title: Add Options and Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, summarize how to add query timeouts, statistics, visualization, and partial failure handling to a Java logs query.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Package Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, create a migration checklist from azure-monitor-query to the newer logs and metrics packages for an existing Java service.

output_examples.input: How do I query AzureActivity by workspace for the last week?
output_examples.output: The response would explain that LogsQueryClient targets a workspace ID, uses a Kusto query, and sets a seven-day query interval.

output_examples.input: How can I read metrics for one Azure resource?
output_examples.output: The response would describe using MetricsQueryClient with a resource ID, metric names, optional aggregations, and a time granularity.

output_examples.input: Should I use this package for a new service?
output_examples.output: The response would note that the package is deprecated and recommend evaluating the newer logs and metrics packages first.

best_practices: Use the newer split Azure Monitor packages for new Java projects when possible.
Limit Kusto result size with projections, time ranges, and row limits.
Handle partial failures and HTTP errors before processing query results.
anti_patterns: Starting a new service on the deprecated package without a migration plan.
Running broad Kusto queries without time limits or projected columns.
Assuming metrics and logs use the same client, response shape, and query options.

faq.question: What package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers com.azure:azure-monitor-query for Java, which Microsoft has deprecated in favor of newer split packages.

faq.question: Can this skill execute Azure Monitor queries?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples. The user must run Java code in their own Azure environment.

faq.question: Does it include authentication guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows DefaultAzureCredential usage, but it does not configure identities, roles, or local credentials.

faq.question: Does it cover both logs and metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes LogsQueryClient, LogsQueryAsyncClient, MetricsQueryClient, MetricsQueryAsyncClient, and MetricsClient examples.

faq.question: Can I use it for sovereign Azure clouds?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes endpoint examples for Azure China Cloud logs and metrics clients.

faq.question: What should I do for new development?
faq.answer: Prefer azure-monitor-query-logs and azure-monitor-query-metrics unless you must maintain existing deprecated package usage.
